title: Proper/open interchange for native bounded constructible Weil complexes
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the abelian categories $\mathcal W_S$ of pro-etale Weil sheaves, their ordinary derived categories, and bounded constructible full subcategories $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(S)$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Consider a commutative square of finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]
$$\begin{array}{ccc}U'&\xrightarrow{j'}&X'\\
p'\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\
U&\xrightarrow{j}&X\end{array},\qquad pj'=jp',$$
where $p,p'$ are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $j,j'$ are quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. The square need not be Cartesian and the schemes need not be separated over $k_0$. Write $J_j,J_{j'}$ for termwise equivariant extension by zero on ordinary derived categories and $Rp_*,Rp'_*$ for total right derivation of the actual equivariant sheaf direct images. Then there is a natural isomorphism of functors
$$J_jRp'_*\cong Rp_*J_{j'}:\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(U')\longrightarrow D(\mathcal W_X).$$
The components and their inverses are morphisms in $D(\mathcal W_X)$, so they include Frobenius compatibility in the native derived realization. This assertion concerns only the stated bounded constructible source; it makes no assertion about arbitrary unbounded $B$-module complexes.

proof.text: Form V=X′×_X U, its open projection b and proper projection q, and the induced map s:U′→V. Since s b=j′ is open and s q=p′ is proper with q separated, s is both open and proper.

proof.text: Lift the existing adic extension-by-zero adjunction to the native IsoAlgebra categories. Localize its termwise exact adjunction to obtain D(j!) ⊣ D(j*), with invertible unit. The unit is degreewise the native sheaf unit.

proof.text: Take the mate of the native direct-image square isomorphism. After forgetting Weil structures it is the existing adic open base-change map, hence invertible for a Cartesian open square. Since open pullback is right adjoint to exact extension by zero, it preserves K-injectives, so this sheaf comparison derives on the unbounded categories.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, proper/open pattern; native proof using the existing source-library comparisons and native proper base change

proof.text: Uniqueness of left adjoints gives (s b)!≅s! b!. The invertible open unit then gives b* j′!≅s!. Since s is clopen, its native extension by zero equals its direct image. Combine this with open base change and composition of native right derived direct images to obtain the natural restriction isomorphism (J_j′ Rp*) j*≅Rp′* on all derived inputs.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, proper/open pattern; native proof using the existing source-library comparisons and native proper base change

proof.text: Construct the reduced closed complement i:Z→X of j. On P=X′×_X Z the projection d has image disjoint from j′ because p j′=j p′. Extension by zero therefore has zero d-pullback, first on sheaves and then termwise on derived objects. For a bounded constructible K, exact constructible open extension makes J_j′K a Weil complex. Apply the existing native proper base-change theorem to this Weil complex and the Cartesian square along i. It identifies i* Rp* J_j′K with a proper direct image of zero, so that object vanishes.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, proper/open pattern; native proof using the existing source-library comparisons and native proper base change

proof.text: For any exact fully faithful open adjunction L⊣R, the counit on an object killed by closed restriction is invertible: its cone is killed by open restriction by the triangle identity and invertible unit, and by closed restriction since both endpoints vanish there. Open and closed pullbacks jointly detect zero objects by cohomology. Apply this criterion to Rp* J_j′K, and combine the counit isomorphism with the natural restriction isomorphism of the preceding step. This assembles J_j Rp′*≅Rp* J_j′ on the bounded constructible full subcategory, as a native natural isomorphism.
